mainTopic: End of the dispute about one offering for many births, the הדרן for פרק שלשים ושש, and the new פרק on מחוסרי כפרה, including the offerings of a גר
overview: The גמרא finishes the dispute between רבי יוחנן בן נורי and רבי עקיבא. Both agree that a woman's offerings work like טבילות, where one can cover many obligations, and they argue only about whether we worry she will become careless. The first פרק then ends with a הדרן. The new פרק opens with a משנה listing four people who are מחוסרי כפרה (זב, זבה, יולדת, מצורע). רבי אליעזר בן יעקב adds a גר and a נזיר. The גמרא explains that זב and זבה are counted separately because the core cause of their טומאה differs, while a male and female מצורע both become טמא through a נגע the size of a גריס. It then explains why the first תנא leaves out a גר and a נזיר: their offerings do not permit eating קדשים. Finally, a ברייתא sets out a גר's offerings: an עולה and שלמים, a single animal, or a pair of birds that are both עולות, but not a מנחה.

steps.title: One guilt offering cannot cover five
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the earlier explanation. Someone who owes five אשמות תלויין is not exempted by bringing just one, because a ברייתא says that wherever sins are counted separately for חטאות, they are also counted separately for אשמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who owes five provisional guilt offerings: when he brings one, is he exempt from the rest? But a ברייתא teaches that this is the rule: whenever sins are counted separately for sin offerings, they are also counted separately for guilt offerings!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the explanation it had just suggested for the dispute. It shows that, with regular offerings, one offering does not cover several separate obligations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If her offerings worked like regular sacrifices, one offering could not free her from many obligations. A ברייתא sets the rule: if each act needs its own חטאת when the sin is certain, each act also needs its own אשם תלוי when it is uncertain. So the comparison to regular offerings cannot explain why one offering is enough for her.

keyTerms.meaning: Provisional guilt offering, brought when a person is unsure whether he sinned
Sin offering, brought for a sin a person knows he did by accident
This is the general rule
Counted separately, so each act needs its own offering
Is exempt

phrases.english: Five provisional guilt offerings,
phrases.notes: This picks up mid-sentence. It means someone who is obligated to bring five of them.

phrases.english: when he brings one, is he exempt?
But isn't it taught: this is the rule:
wherever they are counted separately for sin offerings,
they are counted separately for guilt offerings!

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי מַיְיתֵי חַד מִי מִיפְּטַר? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation of the dispute that the גמרא suggested just before this passage
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the dispute rests on comparing her offerings to regular sacrifices
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With regular offerings, separate sins need separate offerings, as the ברייתא's rule shows. So one offering could never cover several obligations under that comparison.

steps.title: Everyone compares to immersions; the argument is about carelessness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new explanation. Both sages agree that her offerings work like טבילות, where one can cover many. They argue only about whether we worry she will become careless (פשיעה).
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, everyone compares them to immersions. They disagree about whether we worry about carelessness. רבי יוחנן בן נורי holds that we do worry about carelessness, and רבי עקיבא holds that we do not worry about carelessness.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the first explanation failed, the גמרא offers a new one. On the basic law, both sages agree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With טבילה, one immersion purifies a person from many impurities at once. Both sages agree her offerings work the same way, so by Torah law one offering is enough. The only argument is whether the רבנן add a safeguard: רבי יוחנן בן נורי worries that she will treat her obligations lightly in the future, and רבי עקיבא does not share that worry.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; the גמרא drops the old explanation and gives a new one
Everyone agrees
Immersion in a מקוה; one immersion can cover several impurities
Carelessness or negligence
We are concerned about, so we make a safeguard
They disagree about

steps.whatToRemember: Both sages agree that by Torah law one offering can cover her many obligations, just as one טבילה covers many. The argument is only about a safeguard against future carelessness.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יוחנן בן נורי holds that the Torah requires more. He agrees on the basic law and only adds a precaution because of the worry about carelessness.

phrases.english: Rather, everyone agrees
that we compare them to immersions,
phrases.notes: "Them" means her offerings for her many births or זיבות.

phrases.english: and they disagree about whether we worry about carelessness.
Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri holds:
we worry about carelessness,
and Rabbi Akiva holds:
we do not worry about carelessness.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לִטְבִילוֹת מְדַמֵּי לְהוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation that step 1 knocked down
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines what the dispute is about: not the basic law, but a safeguard
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sages argued over whether her offerings are like regular sacrifices or like immersions
steps.terutzMaskana: Both compare to immersions. They argue only over the worry about carelessness.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק שלשים ושש
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the first פרק of מסכת כריתות, called שלשים ושש.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, "Thirty-six."
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the first פרק of the מסכת. It is not part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each פרק is named after its opening words. This פרק opened with the list of thirty-six sins that carry כרת, so it is called שלשים ושש.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you; the formula said at the end of each פרק

phrases.english: We will return to you, "Thirty-six"

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The first פרק of כריתות is finished.

steps.title: New chapter: four lacking atonement, four who bring for deliberate sin
steps.stepSummary: The new פרק opens with two lists. There are four people who are מחוסרי כפרה, and four who bring an offering for a deliberate sin (זדון) just as for an accidental one (שוגג).
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: There are four people who lack atonement, and four who bring an offering for a deliberate sin just as for an accidental sin.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens the second פרק by announcing two groups of four. The next lines of the משנה will name them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מחוסר כפרה has finished becoming pure but still has to bring an offering before he may eat קדשים. Usually offerings are brought only for accidental sins. This משנה points out four cases where a deliberate sin also requires an offering.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Lacking atonement; still needs his offering before he may eat קדשים
A deliberate sin
An accidental sin

steps.whyThisMatters: This opening line sets the outline for the whole new פרק. The rest of the משנה and the גמרא explain each of the two lists.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Four lack atonement,
and four bring an offering
for a deliberate sin as for an accidental one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק after the הדרן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are two groups of four: those who lack atonement, and those who bring an offering even for a deliberate sin.

steps.title: The four people who lack atonement
steps.stepSummary: The משנה names the four מחוסרי כפרה: זב, זבה, יולדת, and מצורע.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are the people who are missing atonement: a man with a discharge, a woman with a discharge, a woman after giving birth, and a leper.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה fills in the first list it opened with. It names the four people who are still מחוסרי כפרה until they bring their קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These four have already become טהור through טבילה, but they still may not eat קדשים until their קרבן is brought. That missing step is what מחוסר כפרה means. Notice that זב and זבה are listed as two separate items, and the גמרא will soon ask why.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone missing atonement. He is טהור, but he still needs to bring a קרבן before eating קדשים.
A man or woman who became טמא from an unusual bodily discharge.
A woman after childbirth.
A person with צרעת, a spiritual skin affliction.

phrases.english: And these are the ones lacking atonement:
the zav, and the zava,
and the woman after childbirth, and the leper.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the first list that was announced in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: זב, זבה, יולדת, and מצורע are the four מחוסרי כפרה.

steps.title: A convert and a nazirite are also added
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב adds that a גר lacks atonement until the blood of his קרבן is sprinkled, and that a נזיר's קרבנות are what let him drink wine, shave, and become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: a convert also lacks atonement until the blood of his offering is sprinkled for him. A nazirite lacks it for his wine, his shaving, and his becoming impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב adds more people to the list of those still missing atonement: a גר and a נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after a גר has had מילה and טבילה, he cannot eat קדשים until the blood of his קרבן is sprinkled on the מזבח. A נזיר stays bound by his נזירות restrictions (no wine, no shaving, no becoming טמא) until his קרבנות are brought.

keyTerms.meaning: A convert to Judaism.
Sprinkling the blood of a קרבן on the מזבח.
A person who took a vow of נזירות.
The shaving of the head that ends a נזיר's term.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says:
A convert lacks atonement
until the blood is sprinkled on his behalf.
A nazirite lacks it for his wine,
phrases.notes: He means the נזיר may not drink wine yet, until his קרבנות are brought.

phrases.english: and his shaving, and his impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the list from step 5 with an additional opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, a גר and a נזיר are also מחוסרי כפרה until their קרבנות are brought.

steps.title: Why count the זב and זבה separately?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה counts זב and זבה as two cases instead of one.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Why are a זב and a זבה different, so that the משנה counts them as two?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks a question about how the משנה counted. Since the זב and the זבה seem like the same kind of case, why are they listed as two? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both are טמא from a bodily discharge and both bring the same kind of קרבן. So it seems they could have been listed together as one item. The גמרא wants to know what makes them different enough to count separately.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Used to ask why two similar things are treated differently.
Counts or lists.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What is different about a zav and a zava,
that he counts them as two?
phrases.notes: "He" is the תנא of the משנה, who listed them as two separate items.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא זָב וְזָבָה דְּמָנֵי לְהוֹן בִּתְרֵין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how the list in step 5 was counted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why זב and זבה are counted as two separate cases.

steps.title: Their impurity works differently
steps.stepSummary: They are counted separately because their טומאה rules differ: a זב is not טמא באונס, and a זבה is not made טמאה by sightings the way she is by days.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because his impurity is different: a זב does not become impure from an accidental discharge, and a זבה does not become impure by sightings the way she does by days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the טומאה of a זב and the טומאה of a זבה follow different rules, so they are really two different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two differences. First, a זב is not טמא if his discharge came from an outside cause (אונס), but a זבה has no such exemption. Second, a זב can become a זב through three sightings even in one day, but a זבה only becomes a זבה through sightings on three separate days.

keyTerms.meaning: His impurity is different, meaning it follows its own separate rules.
Here, a discharge caused by an outside reason, like illness or food, and not from the body itself.
Sightings: how many times the discharge was seen.
Days: on how many separate days the discharge was seen.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the זב and the זבה just have opposite rules on everything. Each one has its own leniency: the זב in the case of אונס, and the זבה in the case of sightings counted within a single day.

phrases.english: Because his impurity is different,
since a zav does not become impure by accident,
and a zava does not become impure by sightings as by days,
phrases.notes: Three sightings in one day don't make her a זבה. Only sightings on three separate days do.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: זב and זבה are counted separately because their טומאה follows different rules: אונס matters only for a זב, and sightings within one day count only for a זב.

steps.title: Sources from two ברייתות
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from "מבשרו" that a זב is not טמא באונס. Another ברייתא says the תורה ties the male to sightings and the female to days.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: "From his flesh", and not because of an outside cause. And he becomes impure by sightings just as by days, as it is taught: The verse tied the male to sightings and the female to days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two ברייתות to support the two differences it just named.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "מבשרו" ("from his flesh") shows that a זב is טמא only when the discharge comes from his own body, and not from an outside cause. The second ברייתא shows that for a male, the number of sightings counts even within one day, while for a female only the number of separate days counts.

keyTerms.meaning: "From his flesh": the discharge must come from the body itself.
The פסוק made it depend on.

phrases.english: As it is taught: "From his flesh"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:2

phrases.english: and not because of his accident.
And he becomes impure by sightings just as by days,
phrases.notes: The printed text has the round-bracket words; the square-bracket word is the corrected wording, meaning "and he becomes impure."

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: תָּלָה הַכָּתוּב אֶת הַזָּכָר בִּרְאִיּוֹת
phrases.english: as it is taught: The verse tied the male to sightings
and the female to days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the sources for the two differences named in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: The two rules that make a זב's טומאה different from a זבה's.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on "מבשרו" and a ברייתא that the פסוק ties the male to sightings and the female to days.

steps.title: The זבה's rules, the opposite side
steps.stepSummary: By contrast, a זבה is טמאה even באונס, and she does not become a זבה from sightings counted within one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a זבה becomes impure by accident, and does not become impure by sightings as by days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up by stating the זבה's side of each rule. This shows clearly why she is counted as a separate case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the two differences are reversed: on אונס the זבה is stricter than the זב, and on sightings in one day she is more lenient. Since each one is stricter in one area, they really are two separate cases, and the משנה is right to count them twice.

keyTerms.meaning: She becomes impure.

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה counts זב and זבה separately because their טומאה rules cut in different directions: a זב is exempt באונס and counts sightings, while a זבה is טמאה באונס and counts days.

phrases.english: And a zava becomes impure by accident,
and does not become impure by sightings as by days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the contrast by stating the זבה's rules after the זב's sources.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: זב and זבה have opposite rules on אונס and on sightings, so the משנה counts them as two.

steps.title: Male and female lepers also have different rules
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that a מצורע and a מצורעת also differ: the man must do פריעה and פרימה and is forbidden in תשמיש המטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A male and female leper also have different impurity rules. A male leper must let his hair grow wild and tear his clothes, as the פסוק says: "His clothes shall be torn and his head shall be left uncovered." He is also forbidden in marital relations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from the last step. If different rules are a reason to list two cases, then the male and female מצורע should be listed separately too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said זב and זבה are counted separately because their rules differ. Here the גמרא shows that the same thing is true of מצורע and מצורעת. This sets up the question in Step 14: why does the משנה list מצורע only once?

keyTerms.meaning: A man with צרעת, a skin affliction that makes a person טמא
A woman with צרעת
Letting the hair grow wild, a sign of mourning required of a מצורע
Tearing one's clothes
Marital relations

phrases.english: A male leper and a female leper also
have different impurity rules,
since a male leper must let his hair grow wild and tear his clothes,
as it is written: "His clothes shall be torn
phrases.notes: ויקרא 13:45

phrases.english: and the hair of his head shall grow wild."
And he is forbidden in marital relations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reasoning of Steps 8 through 10 against the way the משנה counts its list
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that different rules justify counting two separate cases
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If different rules mean separate counting, then מצורע and מצורעת, who also have different rules, should be counted as two.

steps.title: A woman can be a leper too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that a מצורעת does not need פריעה and פרימה. It begins a ברייתא showing that a woman can also be a מצורעת.
steps.simpleTranslation: A female leper does not have to let her hair grow wild or tear her clothes. As a ברייתא teaches: From the פסוק I would only know about a man. How do I know a woman is included? When the פסוק says "and the leper," that covers two: a man and a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts bringing proof for the woman's different rule. First the ברייתא shows that a woman can be a מצורעת at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase "איש צרוע" (a leprous man) mentions only a man. The next פסוק says "והצרוע" (and the leper) with no gender, so it includes a woman. That leaves a question about why the word "איש" was written, and the next step answers it.

keyTerms.meaning: I would only know (this case), a way of asking how a wider case is included
From where do we know?
The leper, written in the פסוק without saying man or woman

phrases.english: And a female leper does not need to let her hair grow wild or tear her clothes,
as a ברייתא teaches: I only know about a man,
phrases.notes: This comes from "איש צרוע הוא" in ויקרא 13:44, which mentions a man.

phrases.english: how do I know about a woman?
When it says, "And the leper" –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 13:45

phrases.english: here there are two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts proving the woman's different rule mentioned in Step 11
steps.raayaObject: That a woman can be a מצורעת, as background for her different rules
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading the word "והצרוע" in ויקרא 13:45

steps.title: The word "man" teaches the woman's exemptions
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that the extra word "איש" teaches that only a man does פריעה and פרימה. The גמרא adds that a מצורעת is allowed in תשמיש המטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the פסוק say "man"? The פסוק moved the word away from the topic before it and attached it to the topic after it. This teaches that a man lets his hair grow wild and tears his clothes, but a woman does not. And a female leper is allowed in marital relations, as it says: "He shall stay outside his tent for seven days," and not outside her tent.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its proof. Since a woman is already included, the word "איש" must be teaching something new: only the man does פריעה and פרימה. A second פסוק shows that only the man is forbidden in marital relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once "והצרוע" includes a woman, the word "איש" would be extra. So it is read together with the next topic, the torn clothes and wild hair, and limits those to men. The words "outside his tent" mean staying away from his wife, and they are said only about a man.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the פסוק need to say this?
The פסוק moved it away, meaning a word is read with a different topic
The topic stated before
The topic stated after
His tent, understood here as his wife

steps.whatToRemember: Only a male מצורע must grow his hair wild, tear his clothes, and stay away from his wife. A מצורעת is exempt from all three.

phrases.english: If so, why does the פסוק say "man"?
The פסוק moved it from the topic above
to the topic below,
phrases.notes: The topic below is the torn clothes and wild hair in the next פסוק.

phrases.english: to teach that a man lets his hair grow wild and tears his clothes,
but a woman does not let her hair grow wild or tear her clothes.
And she is allowed in marital relations,
as it says: "And he shall stay outside his tent for seven days" –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:8. "His tent" means his wife, so he must keep away from her.

phrases.english: and not "outside her tent."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in Step 12
steps.raayaObject: That a מצורעת is exempt from פריעה, פרימה, and the ban on תשמיש המטה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The extra word "איש" in ויקרא 13:44 and "מחוץ לאהלו" in ויקרא 14:8

steps.title: So count male and female lepers as two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its challenge: since their rules differ, the משנה should list מצורע and מצורעת as two cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore, let us count them as two!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the punchline of the challenge that began in Step 11. Since the rules for men and women differ, the משנה should count them separately, the way it counts זב and זבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 11 to 13 proved real differences between a male and a female מצורע. By the reasoning of Step 8, that should mean two entries in the משנה. Yet the משנה lists מצורע only once.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore
Let us count them as two

phrases.english: Therefore, let us count them as two!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion of the challenge from the proofs in Steps 11 to 13
steps.kashyaTarget: The way the משנה counts מצורע and מצורעת as one case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Different rules caused separate counting for זב and זבה, so the same should apply to the male and female מצורע.

steps.title: Only a difference in the core cause of טומאה counts
steps.stepSummary: זב and זבה differ in what actually makes them טמא. מצורע and מצורעת become טמא in the same way, through a נגע the size of a גריס.
steps.simpleTranslation: With זב and זבה, the core of their impurity is different. With a male and female leper, the core of their impurity is not different: for both this one and that one, it is a mark the size of a split bean.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Only a difference in what makes a person טמא is a reason to count two cases, not a difference in side rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זב becomes טמא by counting sightings, while a זבה becomes טמאה by counting days, so the core cause is different. A male and a female מצורע both become טמא through the same sign, a נגע the size of a גריס. The differences in clothes, hair, and marital relations are only rules about how a מצורע must behave afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: The core cause of their impurity
The size of a split bean, the smallest size of a נגע that makes a person טמא
This one and that one, meaning both

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה counts two cases only when the core cause of טומאה differs. That is why זב and זבה are two entries, but מצורע and מצורעת are one.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the male and female מצורע have the same rules. They do differ in tearing clothes, wild hair, and marital relations. The point is that those differences are not about how they become טמא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule for how the משנה builds its list of people who lack atonement: what separates the cases is the cause of the טומאה, not the rules that follow from it.

phrases.english: A זב and a זבה –
the core of their impurity is different,
phrases.notes: A זב counts sightings and a זבה counts days, as seen in Steps 8 through 10.

phrases.english: a male leper and a female leper –
the core of their impurity is not different,
for both this one and that one, it is the size of a split bean.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the rule for counting cases: only a difference in the core cause of טומאה counts
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any difference in rules would make two separate cases
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a difference in what makes a person טמא makes separate cases. Lepers of both genders become טמא the same way, through a נגע the size of a גריס.

steps.title: Quoting רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's addition of a convert
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the part of the משנה where רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says a גר is also מחוסר כפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: a convert is also lacking atonement, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a new line from the משנה. This sets up the questions that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about the first תנא's list of four (זב, זבה, יולדת, מצורע). Now the גמרא moves to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who adds a גר to the list.

keyTerms.meaning: A convert to Judaism
Someone who still needs to bring a קרבן before he is fully fit for holy things

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
A convert lacks [atonement], etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first תנא's list to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's addition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, a גר is also counted as מחוסר כפרה.

steps.title: Why doesn't the first תנא list a convert?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the first תנא leaves a גר out of his list.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the first תנא, why does he not list a convert?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple question: a גר also has to bring a קרבן, so why is he missing from the first תנא's list?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גר clearly needs a קרבן to finish his conversion. So it looks like he belongs on the list, and the question is why the first תנא does not mention him.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה
What is the reason?

phrases.english: And the first tanna,
what is the reason he does not teach a convert?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנָּא קַמָּא, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא תָּנֵי גֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why the first תנא does not agree to include the גר that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב adds.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the first תנא leaves out a גר.

steps.title: The first תנא lists only those whose offering lets them eat sacrificial food
steps.stepSummary: The first תנא lists only people whose קרבן allows them to eat קדשים. A גר brings his קרבן to become fit to enter the קהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the first תנא makes his list, he lists something that becomes permitted to eat קדשים. A convert brings his offering to make himself fit to enter the community.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the first תנא's list has one specific focus: people whose קרבן lets them eat קדשים. A גר's קרבן has a different purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first תנא's list is defined by what the קרבן permits, and for him that means eating קדשים. A גר's קרבן is mainly part of joining the Jewish people (entering the קהל). So even though a גר does bring a קרבן, he does not fit the first תנא's list.

keyTerms.meaning: Something
Sacrificial food
To make himself fit
To enter the community of Israel

phrases.english: When he teaches [his list],
it is something that becomes permitted to eat sacrificial food;
phrases.notes: The letters in square brackets are the corrected spelling of the word.

phrases.english: a convert, when he brings an offering,
it is to make himself fit to enter the congregation.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָתָנֵי מִדַּעַם דְּמִישְׁתְּרֵי לְמֵיכַל בְּקָדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first תנא lists only people whose קרבן permits them to eat קדשים. A גר's קרבן is to let him enter the קהל, so he is not on the list.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer sets the rule for the first תנא's list: it counts only people whose קרבן permits eating קדשים. The next question about a נזיר depends on this rule.

steps.title: Why doesn't the first תנא list a nazirite?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the first תנא also leaves out a נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a nazirite, why does the first תנא not list him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same kind of question about a נזיר, whom רבי אליעזר בן יעקב also includes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר also has to bring קרבנות at the end of his נזירות. So the גמרא asks why the first תנא does not count him too.

keyTerms.meaning: A nazirite, who took a vow not to drink wine, cut his hair, or become טמא from a dead body

phrases.english: And a nazirite, what is the reason he does not teach [him]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining why a גר is left out, the גמרא asks the same question about a נזיר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the first תנא leaves out a נזיר.

steps.title: A nazirite's offering permits ordinary wine, not sacrificial food
steps.stepSummary: A נזיר brings his קרבן so he may drink ordinary wine (יין של חולין), not so he may eat קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, a nazirite too brings his offering in order to be allowed to drink ordinary, non-holy wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with the same rule as before. A נזיר's קרבן does not have to do with eating קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "in the end" (סוף סוף) mean: even though a נזיר's קרבן does permit something, what it permits is ordinary wine. That falls outside the first תנא's list, which covers only things that permit eating קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: In the end; after all
To become permitted
Ordinary, non-holy wine

phrases.english: In the end, a nazirite too,
when he brings an offering,
it is to become permitted to drink non-sacred wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: סוֹף סוֹף נָזִיר נָמֵי כִּי מַיְיתֵי קׇרְבָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19 using the rule from step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A נזיר's קרבן permits ordinary wine, not קדשים, so he is not on the first תנא's list.
steps.whatToRemember: The first תנא counts only people whose קרבן lets them eat קדשים. A גר (whose קרבן is for entering the קהל) and a נזיר (whose קרבן is for drinking wine) are left out for that reason.

steps.title: Then רבי אליעזר בן יעקב should also list an impure nazirite
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי אליעזר בן יעקב lists a נזיר whose קרבן permits him something, he should also list a נזיר טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who lists a nazirite because his offering permits him something, should also list an impure nazirite!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא turns to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. It challenges him: if a נזיר counts, why not a נזיר טמא as well?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב counts any קרבן that permits something, even ordinary wine. A נזיר who became טמא also has to bring קרבנות. So it seems he should count too, but he is not on the list.

keyTerms.meaning: To permit himself
A נזיר who became impure, usually from a dead body

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer,
phrases.notes: This means רבי אליעזר בן יעקב from the משנה, here called by a shorter name.

phrases.english: who teaches a nazirite, [whose offering is] to permit himself,
let him also teach an impure nazirite!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר דְּקָתָנֵי נָזִיר לְמִישְׁרֵי נַפְשֵׁיהּ נִיתְנֵי נָמֵי נָזִיר טָמֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first תנא's list to a challenge against רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's list.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's list, which includes a נזיר but not a נזיר טמא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If any קרבן that permits something counts, then the קרבן of a נזיר טמא should count too.

steps.title: An impure nazirite's offering restarts his naziriteship in purity
steps.stepSummary: A נזיר טמא's קרבן does not permit anything. It lets his נזירות start again in purity.
steps.simpleTranslation: When an impure nazirite brings his offering, it is so that his naziriteship can begin again in purity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a נזיר טמא's קרבן has a different purpose. So he does not belong on רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pure נזיר's קרבן takes away a prohibition (wine), so it counts. A נזיר טמא's קרבן does not take away any prohibition. It actually brings him back into נזירות, now in a state of purity.

keyTerms.meaning: To take effect; to begin
Being a נזיר in a state of purity

phrases.english: When he brings an offering,
phrases.notes: "He" here is the impure נזיר from the question.

phrases.english: it is to have naziriteship take effect on him in purity.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָא מַיְיתֵי קׇרְבָּן לְמֵיחַל עֲלֵיהּ נְזִירוּת בְּטָהֳרָה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every נזיר who brings a קרבן is bringing it to permit himself something.
steps.terutzMaskana: A נזיר טמא's קרבן restarts his נזירות in purity. It does not permit anything, so he is not counted as מחוסר כפרה.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think a נזיר טמא's קרבן lets him drink wine. It is the opposite: his קרבן puts him back into נזירות.

steps.title: A convert may eat sacrificial food after bringing just one bird
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a גר may not eat קדשים until he brings his pair of birds (קן). If he brings even one bird in the morning, he may eat קדשים that evening.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: a convert is held back from eating קדשים until he brings his pair of birds. If he brought one bird in the morning, he may eat קדשים in the evening.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about the details of a גר's קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first says a גר needs his קן before eating קדשים. Then it adds that one bird is already enough for this. He does not have to wait until he brings both birds.

keyTerms.meaning: Held back; prevented
His pair of birds (קן) brought as a קרבן
A single young bird
In the morning

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A convert is held back from eating sacrificial food
until he brings his pair of birds;
if he brought one young bird in the morning,
he may eat sacrificial food in the evening.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן גֵּר מְעוּכָּב לֶאֱכוֹל בְּקָדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a ברייתא with the practical details of a גר's קרבן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גר may not eat קדשים until he brings his קן, but one bird is enough to allow him to eat.

steps.title: Both of a convert's birds are burnt offerings
steps.stepSummary: Everywhere else in the תורה, a pair of birds is one חטאת and one עולה. For a גר, both birds are עולות.
steps.simpleTranslation: All the pairs of birds in the תורה are one sin offering and one burnt offering. Here, both are burnt offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and points out something special about a גר's pair of birds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a pair of birds is split: one bird is a חטאת and the other is an עולה. A גר's pair is different, because both birds are עולות.

keyTerms.meaning: Pairs of birds brought as קרבנות
Sin offering
Burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח

phrases.english: All the bird pairs in the Torah:
one is a sin offering and one is a burnt offering;
here, both of them are burnt offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַקִּינִּין שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה אֶחָד חַטָּאת וְאֶחָד עוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with another detail about a גר's קן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גר's pair of birds is unusual: both birds are עולות.
steps.whatToRemember: A גר may eat קדשים after bringing just one bird, and both birds of his pair are עולות, unlike every other pair of birds in the תורה.

steps.title: Which offerings a convert may bring
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: one animal offering works, an עולה with שלמים works, but a מנחה with שלמים does not. The pair of birds was only allowed as a leniency.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a convert brought his obligation from an animal, he has fulfilled it. If he brought a burnt offering and a peace offering, he has fulfilled it. If he brought a meal offering and a peace offering, he has not. חכמים only mentioned a pair of birds to make it easier for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from Step 23 continues and lists other offerings a גר can bring instead of the birds, and one combination that does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The birds are the cheapest option, but they are not the only one. A single animal, or an עולה together with שלמים, also works. A מנחה paired with שלמים does not, and the גמרא will now ask why.

keyTerms.meaning: his obligation, meaning the offering he must bring
he has fulfilled his obligation
burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח
peace offering, shared between the מזבח, the כהנים and the owner
meal offering, made of flour
to make it easier, as a leniency

phrases.english: If he brought his obligation from an animal – he has fulfilled it,
a burnt offering and a peace offering – he has fulfilled it,
a meal offering and a peace offering – he has not fulfilled it.
They only mentioned a pair of birds in order to make it easier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא about the גר's birds
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A single animal, or an עולה with שלמים, works for a גר. A מנחה with שלמים does not. The birds are only a leniency.

steps.title: Why a meal offering with a peace offering fails
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what is different about a מנחה with שלמים that it does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about a meal offering and a peace offering, that he has not fulfilled his obligation with them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the last ruling of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two offerings are being brought, just as with an עולה and שלמים, so why does this pair fail? The גמרא wants the source for this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: what is different

phrases.english: What is different about a meal offering and a peace offering
that he has not fulfilled his obligation?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא מִנְחָה וּשְׁלָמִים דְּלֹא יָצָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ruling in Step 25
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for why a מנחה with שלמים does not count for a גר

steps.title: A convert must bring what our ancestors brought
steps.stepSummary: From the פסוק "כאשר תעשו כן יעשה": just as our ancestors brought an עולה and שלמים, a גר must bring an עולה and שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written: "As you do, so he shall do." Just as you brought a burnt offering and a peace offering, so too a convert brings a burnt offering and a peace offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק ties the גר's offerings to the offerings our ancestors brought, which were an עולה and שלמים, not a מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גר copies the pattern of the Jewish people when they entered the covenant. Since there was no מנחה in that pattern, a מנחה cannot take the place of the עולה.

keyTerms.meaning: as you do, so he shall do
a convert

steps.whatToRemember: A גר's offerings follow the model of the Jewish people at הר סיני: an עולה and שלמים.

phrases.english: As it is written: "As you do, so he shall do,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:14

phrases.english: just as you brought a burnt offering and a peace offering –
phrases.notes: "You" means the Jewish people entering the covenant at סיני (שמות 24:5).

phrases.english: so too a convert brings a burnt offering and a peace offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 26
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק requires a גר to bring an עולה and שלמים like our ancestors, so a מנחה does not qualify.

steps.title: Then one animal should not be enough
steps.stepSummary: If the גר must copy the עולה and שלמים, how can a single animal offering be enough, as the ברייתא said?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, one animal offering for his obligation should not be enough for him by itself, since it is written: "As you do, so he shall do"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses its own answer to attack the first ruling of the ברייתא, which allowed one animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 27 said the גר needs two offerings, an עולה and שלמים. But the ברייתא in Step 25 said a single animal is enough, so the two seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: if so
it should be enough
by itself

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, חוֹבָתוֹ אַחַת מִן הַבְּהֵמָה
phrases.english: If so, one offering from an animal for his obligation
should not be enough for him by itself,
since it is written: "As you do, so he shall do"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, חוֹבָתוֹ אַחַת מִן הַבְּהֵמָה לָא תִּיסְגֵּי עֲלֵיהּ בְּגַוֵּויהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the answer of Step 27 against the ברייתא's first ruling
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that one animal offering is enough
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק requires both an עולה and שלמים, so one animal alone should not work.

steps.title: רב פפא: if a bird works, surely an animal does
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers with a קל וחומר: the cheaper bird עולה was allowed, so the more valuable animal עולה is surely allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: One can say that a bird was included, so is it not all the more so that an animal burnt offering is included?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא explains why a single animal עולה works even though the פסוק speaks of two offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה already allowed the גר a bird עולה, the cheapest option. An animal עולה is more valuable than a bird, so it surely works too. This is a קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: one can say
was included (by the פסוק)
all the more so
bird

phrases.english: רב פפא said: One can say:
A bird was included,
is an animal burnt offering not all the more so included?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא, יֵשׁ לוֹמַר: לְעוֹף אִיתְרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 28
steps.terutzResolutionType: קל וחומר from the bird offering
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק requires two offerings, so one animal should not be enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since a bird עולה was included, an animal עולה is surely included.

steps.title: Then a meal offering should work too
steps.stepSummary: If cheaper options are allowed by logic, a מנחה should also be enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, even a meal offering should also work!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב פפא's logic, saying it would also allow a מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the bird shows the תורה is lenient with a גר, a מנחה could also be included. That would contradict the ברייתא, which said a מנחה with שלמים does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: if so

phrases.english: If so, even a meal offering should also work!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's קל וחומר from Step 29
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If leniency extends beyond the two offerings, a מנחה should also qualify, against the ברייתא.

steps.title: The word "כן" excludes a meal offering
steps.stepSummary: The word "כן" ("so") in the פסוק limits the options and rules out a מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse limited it with the word "so."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a word in the פסוק itself excludes a מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "כן" means the גר must do the same as the Jewish people, not something lesser. The bird was specially included, but a מנחה stays excluded.

keyTerms.meaning: the verse excluded
so, in the same way

steps.whatToRemember: An animal עולה works through a קל וחומר from the bird, but a מנחה is excluded by the word "כן."

phrases.english: The verse limited it: "so."
phrases.notes: "So" means exactly as you did, which rules out a lesser offering like a מנחה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 30
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קל וחומר should also allow a מנחה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word "כן" excludes a מנחה, so only the bird and the animal are added.

steps.title: Where is the bird offering included?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that a bird עולה is a valid offering for a גר. רב פפא's קל וחומר depended on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where was the bird included?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא's argument in step 29 relied on the bird עולה being allowed. Now the גמרא asks where we learn that. This question sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר said that if the cheap bird is allowed, the expensive animal surely is. That only works if the bird option has a real source. Here the גמרא checks the starting point of that argument.

keyTerms.meaning: Bird (here, a bird brought as a קרבן)
Where
Was included (by a word or phrase in the פסוק)

phrases.english: And the bird, where was it included?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the starting point of רב פפא's קל וחומר and asks for the source of the bird option.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that a bird עולה counts as a valid offering for a גר.

steps.title: The ברייתא repeats the basic rule for a גר
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא opens with the basic rule: just as our ancestors brought an עולה and שלמים, so does a גר. It supports this with "ככם כגר".
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: "As you do, so shall he do." Just as you brought an עולה and שלמים, he too brings an עולה and שלמים, as it says: "As you, so is the גר."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts answering by quoting a ברייתא. Its opening repeats the basic rule we already learned, which sets up the part about the bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This opening is the same base rule from step 27, but the ברייתא needs it as its foundation. It adds the פסוק "ככם כגר" to show that the גר is treated exactly like the Jewish people were. The new information, the bird, comes in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as... so too (a pattern that compares two things)
"As you, so is the גר": the גר is treated like the rest of the Jewish people

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
"As you do, so shall he do":
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:14

phrases.english: just as you brought a burnt offering and peace offerings,

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן כַּאֲשֶׁר תַּעֲשׂוּ כֵּן יַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to step 32 by quoting the ברייתא, starting from its base rule.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא first sets the base: a גר brings an עולה and שלמים, like our ancestors did.

steps.title: The bird עולה is included because it is entirely for ה׳
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא includes the bird from "אשה ריח ניחח לה׳". Something that goes completely to ה׳ is the bird עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we include the bird? The פסוק says: "A fire offering, a pleasing aroma to ה׳." What is something that is entirely for ה׳? You must say, this is the bird עולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the actual source for the bird. The phrase "to ה׳" points to an offering that goes entirely to ה׳, and that is the bird עולה. This answers the question from step 32.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic rule spoke about an animal עולה and שלמים. The extra words "אשה ריח ניחח לה׳" add a further option. The ברייתא reads them as an offering that is completely for ה׳, which it identifies as the bird עולה. This gives רב פפא's קל וחומר the source it relied on.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we include (an extra case)?
The פסוק teaches (introduces the source)
A fire offering, a pleasing aroma to ה׳
You must say (this is the only fitting answer)
A bird brought as an עולה

steps.whatToRemember: A גר's basic offering is an עולה and שלמים. A bird עולה is also included, from "אשה ריח ניחח לה׳", because it goes entirely to ה׳. That is the source behind רב פפא's קל וחומר.
